reasoning: Both attempts keep the behavior unchanged, both pass all three tools, and both keep the bare return in getTallest. A wins on typing and structure. Its price lookup is typed optional, which is what the rubric asks for, and it has a single source of truth for block types. It also uses clean continue guards. B duplicates the type list against the map and repeats the Position checks. It also types the cost map as non-optional and adds an any cast. A's one drift, error instead of assert, only changes an error message, so it outweighs none of this.

criteria.note: The Lune equivalence check passes, and Counts, the > BULK_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD test, the format strings and compare's tie-break all match. Switching assert to error(...) adds a position prefix to the non-table error message, a small drift on an error path.

Names are spelled out, constants are named, and the nested ifs became continue guards. summarize and getTallest still filter separately: getTallest uses isTallestCandidateType and summarize does an inline BLOCK_COSTS lookup.
fmt is split into local formatWholeNumber and formatTenths, and no global remains.
The mixed table is replaced by one BLOCK_COSTS map, and variety now counts keys in counts instead of walking a separate list. The numeric-Type quirk is kept on purpose, but only in getTallest.

It runs under --!strict with exported Block and Summary types, and BLOCK_COSTS: { [string]: number? } makes the missing-price case an optional the code has to handle. It keeps the bare return in getTallest, which the rubric asked to remove.
Only PlotStats.luau changed, the comments are accurate, and luau-lsp, selene and StyLua all pass.
The Lune equivalence check passes, and the original assert and its message are kept exactly.

Names, constants, section headers and a pluralize helper all help. The Position check is repeated, though: position ~= nil and isKnownBlock(block) when isKnownBlock already checks Position, and isTallestCandidate checks it a second time.
There are local formatWholeNumber, formatOneDecimal and pluralize helpers, and no global remains.
The data is split into a BLOCK_TYPES list and a BLOCK_COSTS map, but they have to be kept in sync by hand, as the comment itself warns.

BLOCK_COSTS is typed { [string]: number }, not optional, so cost += BLOCK_COSTS[block.Type] relies on an earlier check instead of handling nil. There is also a local blockType: any cast, and the bare return is kept.
Only PlotStats.luau changed, the comments are thorough and accurate, and all three tools pass.

strengths: Guard clauses with continue keep the loops flat.
The block types live in one place, BLOCK_COSTS, and both the type count and the all-types bonus are derived from it.
The price lookup is typed as optional, so the nil case is checked rather than assumed.
The returned table is named Module, following the project convention.
weaknesses: The bare return in getTallest is still there.
Using error instead of assert changes the error message text slightly.
The filter logic is not fully shared between summarize and getTallest.

strengths: The original assert behavior is preserved exactly.
Clear section headers and documentation of the public API.
The pluralize helper removes the repeated singular/plural logic.
weaknesses: The type list and cost map are two tables that must be kept in sync.
The Position check is redundant across the helpers and their callers.
The price lookup is not optional-typed, and there is an any cast.
The bare return is kept, and the module is not named Module.
